title: Add cross-cohort escalation CI adapter and metric-smoothing middleware
author: Sofia Patel
release_notes: Added a CI adapter that detects asymmetric cohort regressions and an EWMA-based smoothing layer to reduce flapping alerts. Default escalation posts to #eval-escalations and opens a Linear issue when persistent.
description:
Motivation: We keep seeing transient cohort-level blips (e.g. a model that regresses on a narrow customer cohort but looks fine in aggregate). These cause noisy CI failures and pager fatigue. This PR introduces two related capabilities: (1) a cross-cohort escalation CI adapter that computes pairwise cohort deltas and triggers an escalation only when a regression is asymmetric and persistent; and (2) a metric-smoothing middleware (EWMA) applied to per-cohort time series to reduce false positives from single-run jitter.

What this does: The adapter runs as part of eval CI after metric aggregation. For each prompt-set cohort we track the configured baseline and compute delta vs baseline and vs other cohorts. A regression is escalated only when: (a) delta exceeds the cohort threshold, (b) gap vs nearest-cohort > directional gap threshold, and (c) smoothed anomaly persists for N consecutive runs (hysteresis window). When escalated the adapter will (by default) post a compact summary to #eval-escalations, attach recent cohort time-series graphs, and create a Linear ticket (ENG-2468) with metadata and priority.

Key design points: EWMA smoothing uses configurable alpha per-metric; we chose alpha=0.25 default after offline analysis to balance reactivity and noise suppression. Hysteresis defaults to 3 runs to avoid single-run flapping. The escalation adapter is pluggable and can be enabled per-prompt-set via eval config (eval.yaml). We include rate-limiting to avoid duplicate tickets during infra noise and an allowlist for cohorts that should never auto-escalate (e.g., experimental cohorts).

Backward compatibility: Default behavior preserves current aggregated CI gating when the adapter is disabled. The smoother middleware is behind a feature flag so teams can opt in per-prompt-set. No changes to existing metric schema were made.

Testing and validation: Added unit tests that simulate synthetic cohort drifts and verify hysteresis behavior. Integration run against historical eval runs (backfill harness) shows a 62% reduction in noisy escalations on a held-out slice. CI pipeline had an initial flaky integration test which was stabilized by increasing test fixture seed determinism.

Rollout plan: Start with opt-in for a single critical prompt-set (search-safety-cohort) for 2 weeks, then expand to all production prompt-sets if alerts remain low. Ops action required: add webhook token for Linear and ensure #eval-escalations channel exists.
